nodes.title: Katz's p-adic modular functions and the q-expansion principle
nodes.statement: For a p-adic ring A (A = lim A/pⁿA) and N = N₀pʳ with p ∤ N₀, V(N; A) is the ring of functions on isomorphism classes of triples (E, φ, i) over p-adic A-algebras — E an elliptic curve, φ : Ê ≅ Ĝ_m a trivialisation, i a level structure compatible with φ — compatible with base change; W(N; A) ⊂ V(N; A) is the subring of functions whose values at the trivialised Tate curves lie in A[ζ_{N₀}][[q^{1/N₀}]]. Evaluation at the Tate curve embeds V(N; A) in A((q)) with A-flat cokernel (the q-expansion principle), V(N; A) = V(N₀; A), and classical forms embed via ω = φ^*(dx/x).
hypotheses: p-adic rings in Hida's sense; the moduli of trivialised elliptic curves over p-adic rings is imported (ModularCurvesPartII R13.2 and Katz's theory of the Igusa tower).
proofSteps: Define V(N; A) functorially on trivialised triples; the Tate curve Tate(q) over ℤ_p((q))^ carries the canonical trivialisation.
q-expansion principle (1.8a–c): injectivity into A((q)), stability under change of A and A-flatness of the cokernel.
The compatibility condition (1.6) makes a level-N structure on a trivialised curve equivalent to a level-N₀ one, so V(N; A) = V(N₀; A).
Classical forms of weight k embed by evaluating on (E, ω = φ^*(dx/x)) (1.11).
acceptance: The q-expansion principle is stated with A-flat cokernel, not only injectivity.
The p-power part of the level disappears for p-adic modular functions (V(N; A) = V(N₀; A)).

nodes.title: p-adic modular forms are limits of classical forms (Katz)
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5 or N₀ ≥ 3: W(N; ℤ_p) = W(N₀; ℤ_p) equals the p-adic closure M̄(N; ℤ_p) of ⊕_k M_k(Γ₁(N₀); ℤ_p) in ℤ_p[[q]], and modulo p, W(N₀; F_p) ≅ G(Γ₁(N₀); F_p)/(E_{p−1} − 1), where G is the graded algebra of mod-p modular forms of all weights; the isomorphism preserves q-expansions.
hypotheses: Hypothesis N₀ ≥ 3 or p ≥ 5 (Katz's Theorem 1.1).
proofSteps: Katz's Theorem 1.1 at full level Γ(N₀), from the Igusa tower being the étale Galois cover of the ordinary locus with group Γ = 1 + pℤ_p (Katz [16] §2, Theorems 2.1–2.2).
Descend to Γ₁(N₀) with the trace Tr(f) = N₀⁻¹ Σ_{u ∈ U₀} f|u, which is uniformly continuous and fixes E_{p−1} − 1 (Corollary 1.2).
acceptance: The mod-p statement uses the Hasse invariant E_{p−1} ≡ 1: it is the reason p-adic weights are congruent mod p − 1.

nodes.title: Hecke operators and the weight action on p-adic modular forms
nodes.statement: On M̄(N; 𝒪_K) (N divisible by p) the operators T(ℓ) and T(ℓ, ℓ) are defined by Hida's q-expansion formulas (1.13), agreeing with the classical operators on each M_k(Γ₁(N); 𝒪_K); they are p-adically contracting (|f|T(ℓ)|_p ≤ |f|_p), hence extend to the p-adic closure. The profinite group Z = ℤ_p^× × (ℤ/N₀)^× acts continuously by (f|z)(E, φ, i) = f(E, z_p⁻¹φ, z₀i), which on weight-k forms is z_p^k times the diamond action.
hypotheses: N divisible by p; the weight action is through Katz's modular interpretation.
proofSteps: Check (1.13) against the classical formulas on each weight, then extend by uniform continuity.
(1.12): on weight k, f|z = z_p^k f|γ with γ ∈ Γ₀(N) of lower-right entry ≡ z₀.
acceptance: T(p) = U_p for p | N; its q-expansion is a(n, f|U_p) = a(np, f).

nodes.title: Hida's universal Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: H_j(N; 𝒪_K) is the 𝒪_K-subalgebra of End(M_j(N; 𝒪_K)) generated by the T(ℓ), T(ℓ, ℓ), where M_j = ⊕_{k≤j} M_k; the restriction maps H_{j+1} → H_j are surjective and H(N; 𝒪_K) := lim_j H_j(N; 𝒪_K) is a compact ring acting faithfully and continuously on M̄(N; 𝒪_K). nodes.title: The weight algebra Λ and arithmetic points
nodes.statement: Let Γ = 1 + pℤ_p with generator u = 1 + p and Λ_𝒪 = 𝒪[[Γ]] ≅ 𝒪[[X]] (γ = u ↦ 1 + X). The action of Γ ⊂ Z on M̄(N; 𝒪) commutes with the Hecke operators, making H(N; 𝒪) and H^ord(N; 𝒪) into Λ_𝒪-algebras. For k ∈ ℤ, P_k = (1 + X) − u^k ∈ Λ; the arithmetic specialisation at weight k is reduction modulo P_k. H^ord decomposes over the characters a mod p − 1 of μ_{p−1} ⊂ ℤ_p^× as ⊕_a H^ord(N, a; 𝒪).

Idempotents of ℤ_p[μ_{p−1}] split H^ord by the character a.

nodes.title: Jochnowitz's lemma
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 3 and p ≥ 5, T(p) annihilates the quotients M_{k+(p−1)}(Γ₁(N₀); F_p)/M_k(Γ₁(N₀); F_p) and S_{k+(p−1)}/S_k, where weight-k forms embed in weight k + p − 1 by multiplication by E_{p−1} ≡ 1.
hypotheses: k ≥ 3, p ≥ 5; the proof for Γ₀(N₀) works unchanged for Γ₁(N₀).
proofSteps: The filtration theory of mod-p forms: U_p lowers the filtration of a form of weight k + (p − 1) to at most weight k when k ≥ 3 (Jochnowitz, via the θ-operator and the Hasse invariant).
acceptance: Test: p = 5, k = 4: S₈(SL₂(ℤ); F₅) = 0 so the statement is empty; nontrivial checks start at k + 4 ≥ 12.

nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5, H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) are finite Λ_𝒪-modules, and H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) = H^ord(N; ℤ_p) ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_K.

The Γ-invariants of its p-torsion are finite (Theorem 4.2), so by topological Nakayama over Λ (local with residue field F_p) the dual is cofinitely generated.

nodes.title: Hida's control theorem
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5 and p | N: H^ord(N; 𝒪_K) and h^ord(N; 𝒪_K) are free of finite rank over Λ_𝒪, with rank_Λ H^ord(N, a) = rank_{ℤ_p} M_k^ord(Φ; ℤ_p) for every k ≥ 3 with k ≡ a mod p − 1 (and similarly for cusp forms with k ≥ 2). Restriction induces isomorphisms H^ord(N, a)/P_k H^ord(N, a) ≅ H_k^ord(Γ₁(N₀p), ω^{a−k}; 𝒪_K) for k ≥ j(a), and h^ord(N, a)/P_k ≅ h_k^ord(Γ₁(N₀p), ω^{a−k}; 𝒪_K) for k ≥ 2.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 and p | N; ω the Teichmüller character; the finite-level algebras are those of weight k, level N₀p and nebentypus ω^{a−k}.
proofSteps: Freeness: the dual M^ord(N; T_p) is Λ-cofree because its P_k-torsion has constant ℤ_p-corank equal to the rank of classical ordinary forms of weight k (Theorem 4.2 and the classical dimension count), so the finite Λ-module H^ord has no P_k-torsion for infinitely many k and is free (Λ is a two-dimensional regular local ring) (§5).
Control: (H^ord/P_k)^∨ = M^ord[P_k] is the space of ordinary forms of weight k, level N₀p and character ω^{a−k}, for k in the stated range; dualise.
acceptance: The weight range differs for modular forms (k ≥ j(a)) and cusp forms (k ≥ 2).
Finite flatness is over Λ; do not assume the local components are Gorenstein.

nodes.title: Specialisation to classical ordinary forms
nodes.statement: Let F ∈ S^ord(N, a; Λ) be a normalised Λ-adic eigenform (a Λ-algebra homomorphism h^ord(N, a) → I, I finite over Λ). nodes.title: Critical-slope, critical and θ-critical refinements
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform (cuspidal or Eisenstein) of weight k + 2 and level Γ₁(N), p ∤ N, with Hecke polynomial X² − a_pX + ε(p)p^{k+1} having distinct roots α, β. The refinement f_β (the p-stabilisation with U_p-eigenvalue β) has critical slope if v_p(β) = k + 1; it is critical if the equivalent conditions of criticality-equivalences hold (non-classical overconvergent generalised eigenforms, equivalently the eigencurve is not étale over weight space at f_β, equivalently ρ_f|_{D_p} is split with β on the weight-filtration line); it is θ-critical if f_β lies in the image of θ^{k+1} : M†_{−k} → M†_{k+2}. Critical implies critical slope; for cuspidal f, critical ⇔ θ-critical.
hypotheses: α ≠ β; ρ_f is Bellaïche's preferred representation (crystalline at p, indecomposable).
proofSteps: Record the three notions separately: slope (valuation), criticality (local Galois/eigencurve geometry), θ-criticality (image of θ^{k+1} on overconvergent forms).
acceptance: RS-08: keep 'slope k + 1', 'θ-critical' and 'critical refinement' distinct; ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L3 imports this distinction.

nodes.title: Equivalent forms of criticality
nodes.statement: For a refined form f_β the following are equivalent: (i) M_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) ⊊ M†_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) (non-classical generalised eigenforms); (i′) dim M†_{k+2}(Γ)(f_β) ≥ 2; (ii) v_p(β) > 0 and the eigencurve C is not étale over weight space at x = f_β; (iii) v_p(β) > 0 and ρ_f|_{D_p} is a direct sum of two characters; (iv) the β-line of D_cris(ρ_f|_{D_p}) equals the weight-filtration line. Then v_p(β) = k + 1. For cuspidal f these are equivalent to (v) θ-criticality; for Eisenstein f, (v) always holds.
hypotheses: The equivalences (iii) ⇔ (v) (Breuil–Emerton), (i) ⇔ (iii) for Eisenstein series (Bellaïche–Chenevier) and Coleman's limit control theorem are cited by Bellaïche and not decomposed here.
proofSteps: (i) ⇔ (i′) ⇔ (ii): Bellaïche Lemma 2.9 (étaleness of the weight map at x versus the dimension of the generalised eigenspace of overconvergent forms).
(iii) ⇔ (iv): weak admissibility of D_cris.
(v): Coleman's limit control theorem makes coker θ^{k+1} on the generalised eigenspace equal to S_{k+2}(Γ)(x).
acceptance: Keep the cited inputs visible in hypotheses; they are not proved here.

nodes.title: Which newforms have critical-slope refinements

In case (b) it is critical (hence θ-critical); in case (c) it is θ-critical, and non-critical when p is regular; in case (a) non-criticality is conjectural.

nodes.title: Factorial iterates of a self-map of a finite set stabilise
nodes.statement: Let X be a finite set with m = |X| elements and f : X → X any map. For every n ≥ m, f^[n!] = f^[m!]; the map e = f^[m!] is idempotent (e ∘ e = e); its image is the eventual image ⋂_k f^[k](X); and f restricts to a bijection of that image, whose inverse there is f^[m! − 1]. Equivalently, in the finite monoid of self-maps of X, the powers f^{n!} are eventually constant, with value the unique idempotent among the powers of f.
hypotheses: X finite (no algebraic structure is used); m = |X| ≥ 0, with 0! = 1.
proofSteps: For x ∈ X the orbit x, f(x), f²(x), … has at most m distinct points, so (pigeonhole) there are i(x) < j(x) ≤ m with f^{i(x)}(x) = f^{j(x)}(x); put ℓ(x) = j(x) − i(x) ≤ m. Then f^{a}(x) = f^{b}(x) whenever a, b ≥ i(x) and a ≡ b mod ℓ(x).
For n ≥ m: n! ≥ n ≥ m ≥ i(x) and ℓ(x) | n! (as ℓ(x) ≤ m ≤ n), so f^{n!}(x) = f^{m!}(x) and f^{2·m!}(x) = f^{m!}(x); hence f^[n!] = f^[m!] and e ∘ e = e.

Image: e(X) ⊆ f^[k](X) for k ≤ m!, and for k ≥ m! the chain f^[k](X) is constant from k = m on (a decreasing chain of subsets of an m-element set stabilises after at most m steps), so e(X) = ⋂_k f^[k](X).
On e(X), f ∘ f^[m!−1] = f^[m!−1] ∘ f = e = id, so f is a bijection of e(X) with inverse f^[m!−1] (m! ≥ 1).
acceptance: The threshold is explicit: n ≥ |X|; no bound uniform in a family of sets is claimed.
No group-order averaging and no division by m! is used: the argument works in every characteristic.
Test: on ZMod 6, x ↦ 2x has f^[6!] = (x ↦ 4x), which is idempotent (16 ≡ 4 mod 6).

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary projector on a finite module
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring, M an R-module whose underlying set is finite, m = |M|, and U ∈ End_R(M). The ordinary projector is e_U := U^{m!} ∈ End_R(M). It satisfies e_U = U^{n!} for every n ≥ m (so e_U = lim_n U^{n!} in the discrete topology), e_U² = e_U and U e_U = e_U U. The ordinary part is M_ord := e_U M and the non-ordinary part is M_nord := ker e_U = (1 − e_U)M.
hypotheses: R any ring (not necessarily commutative); M finite as a set, e.g. a finite module over R/I with R/I finite.
U is R-linear; the construction uses only the monoid structure of End_R(M).
proofSteps: Apply factorial-iterate-stabilises to the underlying map of U: U^{n!} = U^{m!} for n ≥ m and U^{m!} is idempotent.
e_U is a power of U, hence R-linear and commuting with U.
acceptance: Changing m to any upper bound N ≥ |M| gives the same endomorphism (U^{N!} = U^{m!}).
A supplied idempotent is not a substitute: e_U is defined from U alone.
Units give e_U = 1 and nilpotents give e_U = 0.

nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M): range e_U = ⨅_n range(Uⁿ) and ker e_U = ⨆_n ker(Uⁿ). nodes.title: U is invertible on the ordinary part and nilpotent on the rest
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M): U maps M_ord and M_nord into themselves; U restricts to an R-linear automorphism of M_ord, whose inverse is the restriction of U^{m! − 1} (m = |M|); and U^m vanishes on M_nord.

proofSteps: U commutes with e_U, so it preserves range e_U and ker e_U.
On M_ord, U^{m!−1} ∘ U = U ∘ U^{m!−1} = e_U = id, giving the inverse.
ker Uⁿ is an increasing chain of subgroups of an m-element group; each strict step at least doubles the size, so it is constant from n = ⌊log₂ m⌋ ≤ m on, and M_nord = ⨆ ker Uⁿ = ker U^m.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of the ordinary decomposition
nodes.statement: For M finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M), M = M_ord ⊕ M_nord with both summands U-stable, U bijective on M_ord and nilpotent on M_nord. Conversely, if M = A ⊕ B as R-modules with U mapping A bijectively onto A and every element of B killed by some power of U, then A = M_ord and B = M_nord; U-stability of B need not be assumed.
hypotheses: M finite as a set; the summands are R-submodules.
proofSteps: Existence: e_U is idempotent, so M = range e_U ⊕ ker e_U; apply ordinary-part-bijective.
Uniqueness: U(A) = A gives A = Uⁿ(A) ⊆ range Uⁿ for all n, so A ⊆ ⨅ range Uⁿ = M_ord; every b ∈ B lies in some ker Uⁿ, so B ⊆ ⨆ ker Uⁿ = M_nord (finite-fitting-comparison).
Since M = A ⊕ B = M_ord ⊕ M_nord are finite, |A|·|B| = |M_ord|·|M_nord| with |A| ≤ |M_ord| and |B| ≤ |M_nord|, so both inclusions are equalities.
acceptance: The comparison is by inclusion and counting; no stability hypothesis on B is used, and U(A) = A (not merely U(A) ⊆ A with U injective on A) is what the statement asks.
Test: U = diag(1, 0) on (ZMod 2)²: the complement B = span(e₁ + e₂) of A = span(e₁) is excluded because Uⁿ(e₁ + e₂) = e₁ ≠ 0.

nodes.statement: Let M' → M → M'' (maps f, g) be exact at M, with M', M, M'' R-modules finite as sets and endomorphisms U', U, U'' such that f U' = U f and g U = U'' g. Then ker g ∩ M_ord = f(M'_ord), and if g is surjective then g(M_ord) = M''_ord. Hence M ↦ M_ord and M ↦ M_nord are exact functors on U-equivariant exact sequences of finite modules.

If g is surjective and z ∈ M''_ord, choose g y = z; then g(e y) = e'' g y = z with e y ∈ M_ord.

nodes.title: The ordinary part is the localization at U
nodes.statement: Let R be commutative, M an R-module finite as a set and U ∈ End_R(M); regard M as an R[X]-module with X acting by U (Module.AEval'). Then M_ord → M → M[X⁻¹] = LocalizedModule (powers X) M, x ↦ x/1, is an isomorphism; equivalently the R[X]-linear map M → M_ord, x ↦ e_U x, is a localization at the powers of X (IsLocalizedModule). In particular every U-equivariant map from M to a module on which the endomorphism is bijective kills M_nord.
hypotheses: R commutative (so that R[X] is commutative and LocalizedModule applies).
proofSteps: Injective: if x ∈ M_ord and X^k x = 0 in M then U^k x = 0, so x = 0 since U is injective on M_ord.
Surjective: y/X^k = (U|_{M_ord})^{-k}(e y)/1 + ((1 − e)y)/X^k, and (1 − e)y is killed by U^m, so its fraction vanishes.
Universal property: X acts invertibly on M_ord, and M_nord is X-power torsion.
acceptance: This is the comparison ACC+ use to identify Emerton's localization definition of ordinary parts with the direct-summand definition at finite level.

nodes.title: Finite quotient systems adapted to an endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let M be an R-module and U ∈ End_R(M). A finite quotient system for (M, U) indexed by a set ι is a family (J_i)_{i∈ι} of submodules of M such that: the family is directed downward (for i, j there is k with J_k ⊆ J_i ∩ J_j); each J_i is U-stable; each M/J_i is finite as a set; ⋂_i J_i = 0 (separated); and every compatible family (x_i mod J_i) is represented by one x ∈ M (complete). Then M ≅ lim_i M/J_i, and the J_i form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for the inverse-limit topology, in which M is compact and U is continuous.
hypotheses: ι arbitrary; the countable case ι = ℕ with J_n decreasing is the one used by Khare–Thorne.
proofSteps: Define the induced endomorphisms U_i of M/J_i by Submodule.mapQ.
Separation and completeness say that the canonical map M → lim M/J_i is bijective.
acceptance: The data are the J_i, not merely a topology: coefficient and level maps must respect them (profinite-projector-natural).

A compact module with a continuous U need not admit a U-stable system: on ∏_{n∈ℕ} ZMod 2 with the left shift, the only U-stable open subgroup is the whole group, and U^{n!} does not converge pointwise.

nodes.title: The profinite ordinary projector
nodes.statement: Let (J_i) be a finite quotient system for (M, U), U_i the induced endomorphisms of M/J_i and e_i = e_{U_i}. There is a unique e = e_U ∈ End_R(M) with e(x) ≡ e_i(x mod J_i) for all i and x. For every x and i, U^{n!}x ≡ e x mod J_i as soon as n ≥ |M/J_i|; thus U^{n!} → e pointwise in the inverse-limit topology. Moreover e² = e, eU = Ue, and e(J_i) ⊆ J_i for all i (continuity).

nodes.statement: Let I be a cofiltered index category and 0 → A_i → B_i → C_i → 0 a natural family of short exact sequences of R-modules with every A_i finite as a set. Entire decay gives N>d with −log|r_n(x)| > n log(r+1) for n≥N on all of B; the maximum modulus principle on the affinoid V gives t with r<t<r+1 such that −log|r_n(x)| ≥ (n−d)log t − log|r_d(x)| for all n on V, with equality only at n=d.

Choose γ1,γ2,δ1,δ2 in log of the divisible closure of |K×| with log r<γ1<γ2<log t and δ1 < −log|r_d| < δ2 on V. Define X by the N Laurent/rational conditions δ1 ≤ −log|r_d(x)| ≤ δ2; −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| ≥ (n−d)γ1 for 0 ≤ n < d (the n=0 condition −log|r_d(x)| ≤ dγ1 is the uniform lower bound for |r_d| on X that the printed range 0<n<d omits); −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| ≥ (n−d)log t for d<n<N (printed as (n−d)t). On X the bound |r_d|≥e^{−δ2} makes r_d a unit, so the ratio conditions are Weierstrass conditions inside a Laurent domain and X is an affinoid subdomain.

Strict neighbourhood: V satisfies every defining inequality strictly, so V⊂X. Let W be the union of the affinoid subdomains {|r_d| ≥ e^{−δ1}}, {|r_d| ≤ e^{−δ2}} and, for each ratio condition, {|r_d| ≥ e^{−δ2}} ∩ {reversed ratio inequality}; the intersection with the Laurent domain where r_d is a unit is needed for these pieces to be affinoid subdomains (a bare condition |r_n| ≥ c|r_d| is not an affinoid subdomain at common zeros of r_n and r_d). Then V∩W=∅ and X∪W=B; the manuscript prints X∩W=∅ and X∪V=B, which are the wrong identities.

Set s=exp(γ2). For x∈X and every n≠d one has −log|r_n(x)|+log|r_d(x)| > (n−d)γ2: for 0≤n<d from γ1<γ2, for d<n<N from γ2<log t, and for n≥N from the entire bound together with the n=0 condition (log|r_d(x)| ≥ −dγ1). Y∈C: once Y→X is finite, Y is open and closed in f^{-1}(X) by footnote 2 (Grosse-Klönne; BGR 9.6.3/3 and 9.5.3/5); alternatively make the pointwise 'no root of norm s' uniform on the affinoid X by the maximum modulus principle to obtain an empty annulus s<|T|≤s' over X.

nodes.title: An admissible cover by finite slope blocks
nodes.statement: The affinoid domains Y of Z that are finite surjective over an affinoid weight domain and open-and-closed in its full spectral preimage form an admissible cover of Z.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
proofSteps: For each truncated Z_r, filter the base by the finite degree-at-least-i loci U_i of Lemma 4.4 (each a finite union of affinoids, U_{i+1}⊆U_i, empty for large i).

Start with the maximal-degree locus U_d: cover it by affinoids V_α, where the degree is exactly d, so Corollary 4.3 gives finite flatness; enlarge each block to a strict neighbourhood X_α with Y_α=f_{s_α}^{-1}(X_α) by Lemma 4.5.

Descend by induction on i: from a witness W with W∩U_i=∅ and W∪⋃X_α=B, cover W∩U_{i−1} (a finite union of affinoids on which the degree is exactly i−1) by new blocks, apply Lemma 4.5 to them, and intersect witnesses to keep a strict-neighbourhood witness for U_{i−1}.

Coverage of f_r^{-1}(U_{i−1}) needs, for the old blocks, f_r^{-1}(X_α)⊆Y_α, which holds because s_α>r; record this in the induction hypothesis H(i), since the printed H(i) only records f_r^{-1}(U_i)⊆⋃Y_α and the printed step ends without checking coverage of points of U_{i−1}∖U_i lying in some X_α.
Conclude that every Z_r is covered by finitely many selected affinoids; since Y∩Z_r is an affinoid subdomain of the affinoid Z_r, the cover is admissible.

nodes.title: A polynomial for each spectral block
nodes.statement: For a connected affinoid weight domain A and a finite-flat spectral block Y of degree d, identify O(Y) with A[T]/(Q₀), normalize Q₀ to have constant term one, and obtain a coprime factor Q of the Fredholm series. Apply the Riesz theorem to obtain the associated finite projective Hecke-stable summand N.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value.
R is a reduced K-affinoid algebra with its supremum norm.
Y belongs to the admissible slope cover.
proofSteps: Take the characteristic polynomial Q_0 (monic of degree d) of the spectral coordinate T acting on the finite projective module O(Y) over the connected affinoid A=O(X); Cayley–Hamilton gives A[T]/(Q_0)→O(Y).

Use the closed immersion of Y in X×B[0,r] and the equivalence of residue and finite-module Banach norms (BGR 3.7.4/1) to prove that A[T]/(Q_0)→O(Y) is surjective; equal ranks make it an isomorphism, so F_A vanishes in A{{T}}/(Q_0) and Q_0 divides F_A.

Normalise Q=a_0^{-1}Q_0 with Q(0)=1 and unit leading coefficient. The source invokes Theorem 3.3 without arguing that Q is coprime to S:=F_A/Q. Supply it: Y is open and closed in f^{-1}(X), so over each point x the roots of Q_x are the roots of F_x lying in Y_x with their full multiplicities; hence S_x has no root in common with Q_x, Res(Q,S) has no zero on Max(A), so it is a unit in the affinoid A and (Q,S)=1 by the resultant-unit criterion.
Apply the exact finite-slope theorem to obtain N with Q*(φ)=0 on N; the projector lies in the closure of A[φ], so N is stable under the commuting Hecke algebra.
acceptance: Prove Q(0)=1 and a unit leading coefficient, and justify coprimality with the complementary factor.

Prove coprimality of Q with the cofactor S explicitly (the source omits it); test on a chart whose fibre over some point has a root of F_x of multiplicity 2 to see why the open-and-closed property is what guarantees full multiplicities in Q_x.
Keep N finite projective; a global basis is not part of the conclusion.

nodes.title: Equidimensionality and components of the eigenvariety
nodes.statement: If the reduced weight space W is equidimensional of dimension n, then the eigenvariety D_φ of Construction 5.7 is equidimensional of dimension n, and each irreducible component of D_φ maps finitely and surjectively onto an irreducible component of the spectral variety Z_φ. Under Chenevier's additional identification of the components of Z_φ, those are Fredholm hypersurfaces cut out by prime Fredholm series and their images in W are Zariski open in components of W.
hypotheses: K is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; the data of Construction 5.7 with every affinoid X⊆W reduced and equidimensional of dimension n.
Irreducible components of rigid spaces are taken in the sense of Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces (Ann. Inst. Fourier 49, 1999), which is imported unread.
The description of the components of Z_φ as prime Fredholm hypersurfaces uses Coleman–Mazur Theorem 1.3.11 over power-series rings, or Conrad's 4.3.2, and is not proved for an arbitrary reduced W.
proofSteps: For a chart Y∈C with connected base X=Max(A), the Hecke image T(Y) is a commutative A-subalgebra of End_A(N) with N finite projective, hence T(Y) is A-torsion-free after every flat base change (Chenevier, Lemme 6.2.10, first assertion).

A finite A-algebra that is torsion-free after flat base change has every irreducible component of its spectrum mapping surjectively onto an irreducible component of Spec A, so it is equidimensional of dimension n when A is (Lemme 6.2.10, second and third assertions; the proof localises at the image of a minimal prime and uses that the fibre is discrete and that a torsion-free quotient forces the image prime to be minimal).

Apply this to A ⊂ A[φ^{-1}] ⊂ T(Y): the affinoid Y has O(Y)=A[T]/(Q) whose map to A[φ^{-1}] is a nil-isomorphism (Lemme 6.4.3: the characteristic polynomial ideal satisfies I^r⊂(P)⊂I), so Y, Max A[φ^{-1}] and D(Y) share equidimension n, and π and the projection to X send components to components.

Glue: an irreducible component Σ of D_φ meets each D(Y) in a union of components (Conrad 2.2.9), its image π(Σ) is an irreducible closed analytic subset of Z_φ (Conrad 2.2.3) of dimension n, hence a component of the n-equidimensional Z_φ (Conrad 2.2.7).

Buzzard's Lemma 5.8 states this result for the general machine and delegates the proof to Chenevier's Proposition 6.4.2; the argument above uses only T(Y)⊂End_A(N) and equidimensionality of the charts, so the delegation is legitimate in Buzzard's generality once the imported component theory is available.
acceptance: State the torsion-freeness and equidimensionality lemma as a purely algebraic statement about finite algebras over Noetherian rings and test it on A=K⟨X,Y⟩ with the nonreduced example of Buzzard p. 33, where T(Z_φ)=R⊕I is finite and torsion-free.

nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree d, p odd, U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) open compact with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p, and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p. Put U^f = U ∩ A_f^×, Z(U_a) = U^f·𝒪_F^×/U^f_a·𝒪_F^× and Z(U) = lim_a Z(U_a); G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F/p^a)^× × Z(U_a) via (a b; c d) ↦ (∏_{v|p}(a^{−1}d)_v, a), and G(U) = lim_a G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U). Z(U) has a maximal ℤ_p-free direct summand of rank δ_F, the ℤ_p-rank of the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F unramified outside p, generated by the reciprocity images x_1, …, x_{δ_F} of elements γ_i^{p^{r_i}}; for each v_i | p the units 𝒰_{v_i} ≡ 1 mod v_i have a free summand of rank d_i = [F_{v_i} : ℚ_p] generated by y^{(i)}_1, …, y^{(i)}_{d_i}. The weight algebra is Λ′_𝒪 = 𝒪[[X_1, …, X_{δ_F}, Y^{(i)}_j]] (δ_F + d variables), and 𝒪[[G(U)]] is a finite free Λ′_𝒪-module through 1 + X_i ↦ x_i, 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ y^{(i)}_j, of rank the index of the closed subgroup H these generate. Its weight-two arithmetic points are the kernels of Λ′_𝒪 → Q̄_p with 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ φ(y^{(i)}_j) and 1 + X_i ↦ ψ(x_i) for finite-order characters φ of (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× and ψ of Z(U); they are Zariski dense in Spec Λ′_𝒪.
hypotheses: p odd; U maximal at p. δ_F = 1 + the Leopoldt defect of (F, p) by class field theory.
proofSteps: G(U) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U): the map is well defined on U⁰_a·A_f^× modulo U_a·𝒪_F^× and bijective by the definitions (Skinner–Wiles p. 32).

Z(U) is (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× modulo the closure of the global units, times a finite prime-to-p part; its ℤ_p-rank is d − rank(closure of 𝒪_F^×) = 1 + δ, which by class field theory is the rank of the maximal abelian pro-p extension unramified outside p.
H ≅ ℤ_p^{δ_F + d} has finite index in G(U), so 𝒪[[G(U)]] ≅ Λ′_𝒪[G(U)/H] is finite free over Λ′_𝒪 = 𝒪[[H]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
Density: in each variable the kernels of 1 + X ↦ ζ (ζ a p-power root of unity) are infinitely many height-one primes; products of such give a Zariski-dense set in Spec Λ′_𝒪.
acceptance: The X-variables see only the ℤ_p-free part of Z(U); the torsion of G(U) (roots of unity, the finite quotient by global units) is not a weight variable.
Nearly ordinary weight space includes the torus (Y) directions; the ordinary one-variable weight space of L0 is the parallel, untwisted slice.

nodes.title: Hida's freeness theorem for definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.3, after Hida [H2, Theorem 3.8].) Let F have even degree, with the definite quaternionic towers M_∞(U), M⁺_∞(U) of OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.1. If every element of U/(U ∩ F^×) acts on D^×\G^D(A_f) without fixed points, then M_∞(U) and M⁺_∞(U) are projective 𝒪[[G(U)]]-modules, hence free Λ′_𝒪-modules, of rank rank_𝒪(M_∞(U) ⊗_{Λ′_𝒪} 𝒪). When the ordinary parts have the same 𝒪-rank on the factors of 𝒪[G(U_a)] belonging to all characters of the torsion of G(U), this rank is rank_𝒪 eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), 𝒪) × #G(U)_tors, as Skinner–Wiles state (E11).
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; the fixed-point-free hypothesis on U/(U ∩ F^×).
proofSteps: Free action: #X(U_a) = #X(U⁰_a)·#G(U_a) and H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)^{G(U_a)}, so the Pontryagin dual of H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is free over 𝒪[G(U_a)] of rank #X(U⁰_a) (R18.3).

e commutes with G(U_a), so the dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is a direct summand, hence projective over 𝒪[G(U_a)]; for b ≥ a its coinvariants under ker(G(U_b) → G(U_a)) are the level-a module, by the free action.

Level independence (eH⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), K/𝒪), OAFML R21.1) bounds the number of generators, so M_∞(U) = lim_a of these duals (OAFML R21.1/ordinary-towers-duality) is finitely generated projective over 𝒪[[G(U)]].

𝒪[[G(U)]] is finite free over the local ring Λ′_𝒪 (totally-real-weight-algebra), so M_∞(U) is projective, hence free, over Λ′_𝒪; the same argument applies to the dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)⁺ and M⁺_∞(U).
acceptance: Downstream (hida-hecke-finite; OAFML R21.2 Lemmas 3.10 and 3.19) only freeness over Λ′_𝒪 is used.
The step Skinner–Wiles call clear (drop e) gives projectivity, not freeness of constant rank over 𝒪[G(U_a)] (E11).

nodes.title: Finiteness of the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra over Λ′
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Corollary 3.4.) Let F have even degree. For every U, T_∞(U, 𝒪) is a finite torsion-free Λ′_𝒪-module; in particular it is a semilocal ring complete for its radical, the product of its localisations at its finitely many maximal ideals.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even.
proofSteps: Choose a prime ℓ ∤ 6 unramified in F such that V = U ∩ U(ℓ) acts freely modulo F^× (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.5, requested from R18.3).
Pullback H⁰(X(U_a)) → H⁰(X(V_a)) is injective and commutes with the traces in a, so M_∞(U) ↪ M_∞(V), compatibly with T_∞(V, 𝒪) → T_∞(U, 𝒪); hence it is a map of Λ′_𝒪-modules.
M_∞(V) is free of finite rank (hida-freeness), so M_∞(U) is finite and torsion-free over the Noetherian Λ′_𝒪.

T_∞(U, 𝒪) acts faithfully on M_∞(U) (each T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts faithfully on eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, dual to its level-a quotient), so T_∞(U, 𝒪) ↪ End_{Λ′_𝒪}(M_∞(U)) is finite and torsion-free; finite over the complete local Λ′_𝒪 makes it semilocal and complete.
acceptance: No freeness of T_∞(U, 𝒪) over Λ′_𝒪 is claimed; only M_∞(V) is free.

nodes.title: Hida's control theorem for nearly ordinary Hilbert forms
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.7, Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5].) Let F have even degree. If λ : T_∞(U, 𝒪) → Q̄_p is an 𝒪-algebra homomorphism with λ|_{Z(U)} = ψε^μ, μ ≥ 0, where ψ and φ = λ|_{(𝒪_F⊗ℤ_p)^×} have finite order, then there is a nearly ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of parallel weight k = (μ + 2)·t such that λ(T(ℓ)) and λ(S(ℓ)) are the T(ℓ)- and S(ℓ)-eigenvalues of the newform of π for every prime ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ = GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}). The kernels of such λ are the algebraic primes of weight k.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ε is the cyclotomic character, viewed on Z(U) through reciprocity Z(U) → Gal(F^{(p)}/F).
proofSteps: For μ = 0 the statement is the weight-two correspondence: λ factors through some T₂(U_a, 𝒪) by the definition of T_∞, and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) acts on the v-good vectors of π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_2(U_a) (Skinner–Wiles p. 37).
For μ > 0 Skinner–Wiles cite Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5] without proof; the proof is recorded as a gap.
acceptance: Weights are parallel here: the torus character φ has finite order. Non-parallel weights need λ|_{torus} algebraic, which Proposition 3.7 does not treat.

nodes.title: Weight-two algebraic primes are dense on every component
nodes.statement: (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.9.) Let Q be a minimal prime of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and 𝒳(Q) the set of algebraic primes of weight 2 containing Q. Then 𝒳(Q) is Zariski dense in Spec(T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q). Consequently, if V ⊇ U and for all P in a Zariski-dense subset of 𝒳(Q) some λ ∈ ℋ(P) factors through T_∞(U, 𝒪) → T_∞(V, 𝒪), then Q is the inverse image of a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪).
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; ℋ(P) is the finite set of λ with kernel P.
proofSteps: T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q is a domain, finite and torsion-free over Λ′_𝒪 (hida-hecke-finite), so Λ′_𝒪 ↪ T_∞/Q is a finite injective extension and Spec(T_∞/Q) → Spec Λ′_𝒪 is surjective (lying over).
Every prime of T_∞/Q over a weight-two arithmetic point of Λ′_𝒪 is the kernel of some λ with finite-order restrictions, hence algebraic of weight 2 (hida-control-nearly-ordinary with μ = 0).

The weight-two points of Λ′_𝒪 are dense (totally-real-weight-algebra). If the closure of 𝒳(Q) were a proper closed subset of the irreducible Spec(T_∞/Q), its image would be a closed subset of smaller dimension containing a dense set, which is impossible.

Corollary 3.9: the λ factoring through T_∞(V, 𝒪) on a dense set put Q inside the closed set cut out by ker(T_∞(U) → T_∞(V))-compatible primes; a minimal prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪) below a generic point pulls back to Q.
acceptance: Skinner–Wiles call the density 'immediate' after the Λ′_𝒪 statement; the lying-over and dimension step is spelled out here.

nodes.title: The ordinary family modular-symbol module M_m
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, N prime to p, T*_N (resp. T_N) Hida's universal ordinary Hecke algebra of tame level N acting on all (resp. cuspidal) forms, and m a maximal ideal of T*_N whose residual representation ρ̄_m is irreducible. For each r ≥ 0 the relative homology sequence 0 → H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H₁(X₁(Np^r), C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → H̃₀(C₁(Np^r); ℤ_p) → 0 (4.1) remains exact on ordinary parts, and after localising at m the reduced H₀ of the cusps vanishes. So M_m := lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r); ℤ_p)^ord_m ≅ lim_r H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p)^ord_m is a module over (T*_N)_m ≅ (T_N)_m. Complex conjugation on X₁(Np^r) commutes with the Hecke action, and M_m = M⁺_m ⊕ M⁻_m.
hypotheses: p odd (for the ± splitting); ρ̄_m irreducible (so the cusps disappear after localisation and (T*_N)_m = (T_N)_m).
proofSteps: The ordinary projector is exact (L0a), so (4.1) stays exact on ordinary parts; Eisenstein maximal ideals carry the cuspidal H̃₀, and at non-Eisenstein m it vanishes.
The transition maps in r are the corestrictions/traces on homology, compatible with the Hecke action; M_m is their inverse limit.
Complex conjugation commutes with T(ℓ), U_p and the diamond operators on homology; 2 is invertible.
acceptance: M_m is integral (over ℤ_p) and defined before inverting p.
At an Eisenstein m the absolute and relative limits differ; the construction is only claimed for irreducible ρ̄_m.

nodes.title: Freeness of M^±_m: the family period line
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.1.) If ρ̄_m is irreducible and p-distinguished, each of M⁺_m and M⁻_m is a free (T_N)_m-module of rank one.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished (the two characters of ρ̄_m|_{G_{ℚ_p}} are distinct).
proofSteps: Wiles [34, Theorem 2.1] with Theorem 2.1.2: J₁(Np)(ℚ̄)[m]^ord is free of rank 2 over T_N/m (requested from ModularCurvesPartII R14.6).
By (4.2), Hom(M_m, ℚ_p/ℤ_p)[m] ≅ H₁(Np; ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ H₁(Np; F_p)^ord_m[m] ≅ J₁(Np)[p][m]^ord, so M_m/mM_m is free of rank 2 over T_N/m.
M_m ⊗ ℚ_p is free of rank 2 over (T_N)_m ⊗ ℚ_p (Eichler–Shimura in each weight), so Nakayama makes M_m free of rank 2, and the ± parts are free of rank 1.
acceptance: Without p-distinguishedness M^±_m need not be free; the family period is then a module, not a line.

nodes.title: Family periods as trivialisations of an invertible module
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of family-symbol-free-rank-one, a family period for the sign ± is an isomorphism θ^± : (T_N)_m ≅ M^±_m (4.3); two choices differ by a unit of (T_N)_m. At a classical height-one prime ℘ of (T_N)_m, θ^± mod ℘ is a generator of the saturated integral period lattice of the eigenform f_℘ (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1), so the single choice θ^± fixes the canonical periods of all f_℘ up to the units of the O(℘), compatibly along the family.
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished.
proofSteps: θ^± exists by freeness; Aut_{T_m}(M^±_m) = T_m^×.
Reduction mod ℘ and control identify M^±_m/℘ with the ±-part of the classical symbols of f_℘ with 𝒪(℘)-coefficients, free of rank one; its generator is the saturated lattice generator of MS L1.
acceptance: A period line is not a globally chosen basis: θ^± is data, and statements depending on it are equalities up to T_m^× (integrally) or up to O(℘)^× at ℘, not up to a field scalar.
Where M^±_m is not free (p-distinguishedness fails) only the module, not a trivialisation, is available.

nodes.title: The two-variable measure of a Hida family
nodes.statement: The paths [∞, a] on X₁(Np^r), a ∈ P¹(ℚ), give classes in H₁(X₁(Np^r), cusps; ℤ_p) compatible in r; projecting to ordinary parts, localising at m and passing to the limit gives a ↦ {∞, a} ∈ M_m. For a + p^rℤ_p ⊆ ℤ_p^×, µ(a + p^rℤ_p) := U_p^{−r}{∞, a/p^r} ∈ M_m (Definition 4.1.2) is additive (Proposition 4.1.3), hence defines L(m, N) ∈ M_m ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]], with ± components L^±(m, N) ∈ M^±_m ⊗̂ ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]]; after a family period it lies in (T_N)_m[[ℤ_p^×]]. Projecting to the ω^i-part gives L(m, N, ω^i) ∈ (T_N)_m ⊗̂ Λ^{(i)} with sign (−1)^i (the other sign projects to 0).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible; U_p is invertible on M_m (ordinary part).
proofSteps: Additivity: U_p = Σ_{b mod p}(1 b; 0 p) acts on {∞, a/p^r} as Σ_b {∞, (a + bp^r)/p^{r+1}}, so µ(a + p^rℤ_p) = Σ_b µ(a + bp^r + p^{r+1}ℤ_p).
ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]] is the ring of ℤ_p-valued measures (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1); the completed tensor product uses the m-adic topology on M_m.
The sign of the ω^i-projection: the involution z ↦ −z on ℤ_p^× corresponds to complex conjugation.
acceptance: U_p^{−r} makes sense because U_p is a unit on the ordinary part; this is where ordinarity is used.
L(m, N) is integral: no denominators are introduced before a period is chosen.

nodes.title: Specialisation to one-variable p-adic L-functions
nodes.statement: (Emerton–Pollack–Weston Proposition 4.1.4.) Under the hypotheses of family-symbol-free-rank-one, for every classical height-one prime ℘ of (T_N)_m, L^±(m, N)(℘) ∈ O(℘)[[ℤ_p^×]] is the analytic p-adic L-function of the normalised eigenform f_℘ ∈ S_k(Np^∞, O(℘))^ord[κ_℘], computed with respect to a canonical period; f_℘ need not be new, so the specialisation may be imprimitive (Euler factors at primes dividing the tame level of an oldform removed).
hypotheses: ρ̄_m irreducible and p-distinguished; ℘ classical of weight k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: The one-variable construction µ_{r,k}(a + p^nℤ_p) = U_p^{−n}{∞, a/p^n} ∈ (M_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} gives L^±_p(m_{r,k}, N).
(M_{r,k})^±_{m_{r,k}} is free of rank one over (T_{r,k})_{m_{r,k}} by control and family-symbol-free-rank-one; the family period induces its trivialisation.

By construction L^±(m, N) ≡ L^±(m_{r,k}, N) mod ω_{r,k}, hence mod ℘; reduction of the latter mod ℘_{r,k} is the p-adic L-function of f_℘ for the canonical period (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L2's ordinary integral measure).
acceptance: The equality is up to O(℘)^× (the canonical period), not up to a field scalar.
For the primitive (newform) p-adic L-function one passes to the branch rings T(𝔞)° (Emerton–Pollack–Weston §4.2), not yet planned.

requests.need: Minimal complexes over a noetherian local ring: every good complex (bounded, finite projective terms) is quasi-isomorphic to a minimal one (differentials zero mod m), and quasi-isomorphic minimal complexes are isomorphic (Khare–Thorne Lemma 2.3); gluing along R_c = R/I_c for open ideals cofinal with mⁿ: the limit of good complexes M_c with M_{c+1} ⊗ R_c ≅ M_c is good with M_∞ ⊗ R_c ≅ M_c and H*(M_∞) = lim H*(M_c), and compatible homotopy classes of maps glue uniquely (Lemma 2.13), with the uniqueness up to homotopy of the glued minimal complex (Lemma 2.14). gaps.title: Formal-model finiteness beyond the existing geometric outline
gaps.detail: Conrad A.1.2 was read through its proof (again by R1-review). It requires Bosch–Lütkebohmert, Formal and rigid geometry I (Math. Ann. 295, 1993), Proposition 4.7 and §3.5 (rig-points, via Conrad's Lemma A.1.5), and II (Math. Ann. 296, 1993), Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 (flat and quasi-finite formal models); those primary proofs remain unread. Its scheme step is Lemma A.1.4, proved by fpqc base change to a henselian local ring, the structure theorem for separated locally quasi-finite maps (EGA IV_4 18.5.11(c)), constancy of rank over the closed fibre and spreading out of finite presentation; this was read but its EGA chain remains unexpanded. Remark A.1.3 notes that the discretely valued case is Abbes–Mokrane Lemme A.1 and that local rings of formal models are not Noetherian for nondiscrete K. R1-review supplier assessment (Task 4): no stage in data/atlas.json explicitly supplies these results in the needed generality. AdicSpacesPartII:R2 constructs admissible formal schemes, admissible blow-ups and the generic-fibre functor but states no flattening, quasi-finite-model or finiteness criterion; AdicSpacesPartII:F0 restricts formal geometry to complete Noetherian adic rings (excluding O_K for nondiscrete K) and only promises properness/separatedness/smoothness comparisons with formal models; AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 supplies admissible formal models 'in the scope required by H1' (étale cohomology); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1 treats nondiscrete valuation bases only for nearby cycles and H1:henselian constructs affinoid henselizations, not the scheme lemma A.1.4; SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1 owns fpqc descent on the scheme side. Closest candidates, in order: AdicSpacesPartII:R2, AdicSpacesPartII:F0, AdicEtaleGeometry:A2, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1. gaps.title: Complete primary modular eigencurve proof (source now acquired, mostly unread)
gaps.detail: The catalogue selects Coleman–Mazur, The eigencurve (1998), DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511662010.003. R1-review acquired the authors' 113-page preprint from the Internet Archive capture (31 October 2008) of Coleman's Berkeley page, https://web.archive.org/web/20081031155820id_/http://math.berkeley.edu/~coleman/eigen/coleman-mazur.pdf, SHA-256 bf8e96f23fb3db2f886a5106547798c6d899941b316f340079b3aabb4ad04a70, fetched 2026-09-15; the live Berkeley URL and Barry Mazur's Harvard page return 404. Read so far: §1.1 (nested spaces, p. 11), Lemma 1.3.10–Corollary 1.3.12 (pp. 24–26), Chapter 7 opening and §7.1 with Theorem 7.1.1 (pp. 91–93: the local pieces D(V) over an affinoid Y of weight space, N(V) locally free of rank deg Q_V, T(V) the image of H⊗A in End_A(N(V)), the q-expansion pairing 0→T(V)→Hom_A(N(V),A)→M→0), §7.4 opening with Lemma 7.4.1 (pp. 101–102), Proposition 7.4.5 (D reduced, nested, components generically isomorphic to Fredholm hypersurfaces, p. 104) and the statement of Theorem 7.5.1 (D ≅ C^red, p. 105). The footnote on p. 91 records that the proof of [C-BMF] Proposition A5.8 works over any K after replacing 'x∈V' by 'closed points x of V', the argument Buzzard's §4 generalises. Buzzard's opening §6 imports these constructions; this packet still does not claim to have read the complete modular proof (Chapters 2–6, §§7.2–7.5 proofs) or to derive the distribution-valued cohomology and critical-point results from the generic machine.

gaps.title: Coherent eigenmodules and nonflat specialization
gaps.detail: The original stages promise the coherent eigenmodule/eigensymbol sheaf, Tor comparisons and generalized eigenspaces. The inspected finite Hecke algebra construction and flat-base-change lemma do not alone prove this entire package. gaps.title: Dimension theorem narrowed; dense classical points still require separate inputs
gaps.detail: Buzzard Lemma 5.8 delegates equidimensionality to Chenevier Proposition 6.4.2. R1-review read that proposition with its proof (author copy glnfam.pdf, internal p. 53), Lemme 6.2.10 (pp. 47–48) and Lemme 6.4.3 (p. 54): the argument uses only that the Hecke image is a commutative subalgebra of End_A(N) for N finite projective over an equidimensional reduced affinoid A, so it applies in Buzzard's generality; the new node equidimensional-components (addedBy R1-review) records it. Remaining imports: Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, results 2.1.5, 2.2.3, 2.2.7, 2.2.9 and 4.3.2, and Coleman–Mazur Theorem 1.3.11 (prime factorisation of Fredholm series over O[[T_1,…,T_m]], now on disk but its proof via Theorem 1.3.7 unread) for the identification of the components of Z_φ; these are needed for the 'components map onto Fredholm hypersurfaces' and Zariski-density clauses, not for equidimensionality. Dense classical points and unitary classicality require the application's actual overconvergent coefficient and control arguments (Chenevier §6.4.5 and §7 for unitary groups; Coleman–Mazur for the modular case). This packet does not infer them from eigenpacket-point classification.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.3 and its proof, pp. 35–36 (Numdam PDF pages 32–33)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 3.3 assumes that each element of U/U∩F^× acts without fixed points on D^×\G^D(A^f). It claims that M_∞(U) and M⁺_∞(U) are free over Λ′_𝒪, with rank rank_𝒪 eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), 𝒪) times the order of the torsion subgroup of G(U). The proof says it suffices to establish this before applying e.
sourceIssues.correction: The argument shows that the Pontryagin dual of eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) is projective over 𝒪[G(U_a)] and that M_∞(U), M⁺_∞(U) are projective over 𝒪[[G(U)]], hence free over Λ′_𝒪, of rank rank_𝒪(M_∞(U) ⊗_{Λ′_𝒪} 𝒪). The stated rank, and freeness over 𝒪[G(U_a)], need in addition that the ordinary parts have equal 𝒪-rank on the factors of 𝒪[G(U_a)] belonging to the different characters of the prime-to-p torsion of G(U_a).
sourceIssues.reason: e is an 𝒪[G(U_a)]-linear idempotent on the free 𝒪[G(U_a)]-module dual to H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪), so the dual of the e-part is a direct summand, i.e. projective. 𝒪[G(U_a)] is a product of local rings indexed by the (Galois orbits of) characters of the prime-to-p part of G(U_a), and a projective module is free of the stated rank only if its ranks on these factors agree; the proof's coinvariant computation sees only the trivial character. The components correspond to nearly ordinary forms with different tame characters at p, whose dimensions the argument does not compare. Corollary 3.4 and Lemmas 3.10 and 3.19 use only freeness over Λ′_𝒪, which the argument does give.
